evidence: ARITHMETIC (holds for a single attempt per judge call). task.toml has [agent].timeout_sec=7200, [environment].build_timeout_sec=600 and [verifier].timeout_sec=13200, all equal to the template and the contract. tests/test.sh is byte-identical to the template (the diff is empty): run_suite gates 1500 (line 213), run_suite scored 11100 (line 224) and rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1 (line 207), so judges run serially. Gates: render timeout 600 + constraints timeout 600 = 1200 < 1500. Scored: functional judge.toml lines 2-4 set 'mode = "individual"' and 'timeout = 600' over 15 criteria. In RewardKit 0.1.7, _arun_agent_individual makes one agent call per criterion, sequentially, each wrapped in asyncio.wait_for(timeout=judge.timeout), so functional takes up to 15 x 600 = 9000 s. Polish (batched) has 900 s and visual (batched) 900 s; 9000 + 900 + 900 = 10800 < 11100, leaving 300 s of slack for 17 agent launches. Gates plus scored: 1500 + 11100 = 12600 < 13200. Liveness: the test.sh probe loop runs 120 x 0.25 s (about 30 s nominal, with 2 s urlopen timeouts). The restart helper's 30 s readiness loop runs inside restart_mcp.py's HELPER_TIMEOUT_SEC = 55, which itself sits inside the 600 s call. The agent image and tests/Dockerfile equal the template (manifest hash 0a75419e... for environment/Dockerfile; empty diff for tests/Dockerfile), so the canonical 600 s build and 7200 s agent budgets are reasonable. DEFECT ('long enough' and the canonical budget). The template and the NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md 'Time budgets' table fix Functional at one batched judge with 9000 s. The frozen task changes it to individual mode with a hard cap of 600 s per criterion. Git HEAD still has 'mode = "batched"' and 'timeout = 9000'; the change is uncommitted in the frozen snapshot. I found no recorded reason, authorization or measurement for this per-call timeout change in qc/README.md, REVIEW_POLICY.md, NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md, TASK_AUTHORING_WORKFLOW.md, handoffs/ or the task itself. As instructed, I did not read earlier rounds' reports. AGENTS.md and qc/README.md require any timeout change to record its reason and authorization, and say 'Current candidate budgets remain unchanged without a measured reason'. The raw-evidence-index.json scope says 'Full configured grading/workload ... absent', and every artifact is labelled 'Not a ... judge-duration measurement'. No runtime-evidence.json record exists for timeouts_fit_the_work. test.sh is frozen with an 11100 s scored budget and polish plus visual take 1800 s, so individual mode with 15 criteria can never give a criterion more than about 620 s. Several criteria are long multi-context browser chains. (1) hro_manager_roles (weight 4): two jobs, 7 cards, about 10 setup moves, about 12 Ingrid actions, replays, Bill's legs, notes and an Observer read. (2) hro_undo (weight 5): 6 cards and 8 steps, with several UI and replay refusals across two people. (3) hro_bulk (weight 5). (4) hro_intake_restart (weight 4.5): 2 jobs, 5 refused jobs, 6+3 candidates, about 6 moves, notes or messages, a restart, and a full comparison in a fresh context. (5) hro_unread_seen (weight 3.5): about 6 timed observations, with up to 3 attempts each. Its negative legs must watch the full 15 s plus a 2 s settle, and fresh-context confirmations span Lena, Rafael, Tomas, Mei, Aud and Bill. (6) hro_candidate (weight 4.5). (7) hro_readonly_roles (weight 4.5). Every individual call also repeats the prompt.md 'Minimal backend check' preamble (functional/prompt.md line 15: sign in, add a candidate, reload, open an independent Observer context), so that work is paid 15 times out of the 600 s caps. The functional prompt never tells the judge its budget. Its line-35 path ('exhausted budget' -> NOT EXERCISED) cannot run on a hard kill: RewardKit's _timeout_scores records 0.0 with the error 'judge timed out after 600s'. Polish keeps the canonical 900 s but batches five heavy rows plus the preamble: up to 12 cards added, two watches of up to 60 s, a session end and resume with Rafael, Mei and Rafael sign-ins, a failed send, and the earlier-place check. A polish timeout zeroes the whole 0.2 polish dimension (Colderwater lesson 11). A latent issue: RewardKit retries a schema-mismatched agent response up to _MAX_JUDGE_RETRIES = 3 times, each with a full timeout, so one criterion can take up to 1800 s. With only 300 s of scored slack and 15 separate calls, one retry can push the suite past 11100 s, and test.sh then exits with no scored reward. The template has the same retry exposure, but individual mode multiplies the number of calls. POSITIVE NOTES. The nesting arithmetic is consistent and preflight confirms it. The shared harness is untouched. Individual mode limits a single overrun to one criterion instead of zeroing all of Functional. Each assembled prompt is small (functional prompt.md 9.9 KB + app_context 1.9 KB + one criterion; polish about 15 KB), far below the 128 KB limit (lesson 10). Lessons 7 and 14 (bounded repeats of void timed attempts) are applied; this caps the cost of a timed observation but also adds to it.
counterexample: A fully conforming app, for example the golden: the judge (claude-code with glm-5.3-flashx) works through hro_manager_roles or hro_undo at a normal pace. That is about 80-120 Playwright steps at roughly 5-8 s each, counting the repeated preamble and the sign-ins in several independent contexts. At 600 s it is still mid-chain, so RewardKit kills the subprocess and records 0.0 ('judge timed out after 600s') for that criterion, which carries weight 4 or 5. The criterion is not marked NOT EXERCISED. Oracle drops below 1, and the model's score is lowered by our harness rather than by its submission. A broken app that fails at an early leg finishes quickly and keeps its score, so the timeout penalizes thorough, correct apps more than weak ones. The same can happen to all five polish rows if the batched polish run exceeds 900 s (12-card setup, two 60 s watches, multi-account session legs). None of this has been measured: no full configured judge-duration run exists for these bytes.
suggested_fix: Either restore the canonical Functional judge (mode = "batched", timeout = 9000), or keep individual mode only after recording its reason and authorization and measuring full configured golden judge durations per criterion and for polish in the verifier image, with margin under 600 s and 900 s. Achieve that margin by cutting browser work per criterion (shorter setup chains, no repeated preamble), not by editing test.sh, and record the measurement as the timeouts_fit_the_work runtime-evidence record.
